blocks.title: Polymorphism
blocks.text: Polymorphism is the ability of different objects to respond to the same method call in their own way: one interface, with specific behaviour for each object.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
def animal_sound(animal):
....animal.make_sound()

animal_sound(Dog())    # Bark!
animal_sound(Cat())    # Meow!

blocks.prompt: Why is animal_sound() an example of polymorphism?
blocks.explanation: The same call, animal.make_sound(), produces different results depending on the object's class, so the function handles Dog and Cat in one uniform way.

items: Polymorphism: one method name, different behaviour per class; animal_sound(Dog()) barks, animal_sound(Cat()) meows.
